app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#0:
Ask mode: search Layer 2, over Cloudflare AI Search.

THE RULE THIS FILE EXISTS UNDER: classic search is D1 and only D1, so with `AI_SEARCH` unbound no
Ask affordance renders and /search is byte-identical to what it was before Layer 2. That off
switch is a requirement rather than a nicety. The corpus is the same section-grained records the
D1 index uses, from the same `records.mjs`.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#3:
How many chunks the answer may draw on.

THE BOUND IS THE ANSWER, NOT THE CORPUS, which is why it does not move: past it, retrieval widens
the net without widening the answer and only dilutes the ranking. A ceiling justified by how much
there is to retrieve goes stale on every publish. No corpus figure appears here, per rule 17.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#8:
Splits the upstream in two, one to the reader and one to an accumulator parsed inside `waitUntil`,
so caching costs time-to-first-token nothing. Null when the generation produced nothing, which
must not be cached.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#10:
Rebuilds a cached answer in the shape the model produces, so the client cannot tell a replay from
a generation: one parser, one rendering path. One delta rather than re-simulated typing, because
pretending to think over a cached string would be theatre.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#12:
Every item in the index, following pagination to the end. `items.list()` IS PAGED and a bare call
returns the first page only, which was invisible while the corpus was small: a prune reported
success for a post whose items sat on a later page, leaving a draft answerable. A prune that
cannot see an item cannot delete it, and reports success either way.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#15:
ONE MARK PER PAGE, and the COUNT of them is the measurement, so round trips are counted rather
than inferred from the index size. Entries, not a map: two pages produce two entries with the
same name, and anything collapsing them by name reports one.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#17:
The posts that may appear in the Ask index.

THE AI INDEX IS A PUBLIC SURFACE, cited by slug, so this is the same kind of gate as
`publiclyVisible()` and must agree with it. THE FILTER HAS TO HAPPEN AT UPLOAD TIME, because AI
Search has no per-item status a query can filter on, which is how the classic index protects
itself. Nothing unpublished may enter at all.

@param posts
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#18:
COMPOSED, NOT RESTATED: a hand-rolled copy agreed with `publiclyVisible()` by inspection and by
nothing else, which is the shape that leaked drafts into Ask.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#20:
Uploads every search record to built-in storage, rather than through the crawler: the crawler
indexes a domain onboarded to this account, and the apex still resolves to the legacy site, so a
crawl would index the wrong site and would lose the heading granularity a citation deep-links to.
Upload is an UPSERT keyed by filename, so re-running is idempotent.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#21:
THE CORPUS COMES FROM D1, materialised by the same `records.mjs` both writers run and read back
with `visibilityClause` composed in the SQL, so drafts and future posts never enter the index.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#24:
THE PAPERS, FROM THEIR TWINS RATHER THAN FROM `search_docs`, which is a split the ruling draws.
The record carries the abstract, which is what keyword search should snippet; what Ask retrieves
over is the PAPER, and the twin has the extracted text. Uploading both would put two documents
about one paper in the index, and the shorter would sometimes win a question the longer answers.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#27:
Every paper's Ask item key, derived from the committed corpus.

FROM THE MODULE, NOT FROM D1, on hard rule 1: every `search_docs` reader must compose
`visibilityClause`, and composing it here would ask a visibility question about a corpus that has
none. Reading the module points the index at the repository, which is rule 18's direction.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#28:
Uploads every paper's markdown twin, and returns the keys it wrote.

FETCHED THROUGH `ASSETS`, which looks indirect and is not: the twins are gitignored build output
so the extracted text stays out of the bundle, and a Worker cannot read a file it does not
import. It has hard rule 7's property anyway: what gets indexed is the document the site actually
serves at that URL.

A MISSING TWIN IS REPORTED, NOT INVENTED, and its key is still returned, because the caller's
prune deletes every key it is not given and omitting it would turn a missing build into a
DELETION.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#29:
Syncs ONE post's records, and drops that post's stale items. A full corpus sync on every save is
correct at seven records and absurd at seven hundred, and section decomposition is a pure
function of one post's markdown, which is what makes this sound rather than a shortcut. The prune
is scoped to this post's keys, so a concurrent post is never touched.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#31:
ONE FAILING RECORD USED TO ABANDON THE REST, and the caller catches by design, so a whole post's
records went missing with the failure nowhere to go. Each record is isolated and retried ONCE.

A FAILED KEY STILL JOINS `live`, WHICH LOOKS WRONG AND IS NOT: the prune deletes every key not in
it, so isolating the loop without this would turn a transient failure into a DELETION of the good
copy already indexed. `live` means "this key should exist", not "this key was just written".
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#36:
Compares what the index holds against what the corpus says it should hold, because the Ask sync
is allowed to fail without failing the save and the save then redirects, so a failure has nowhere
to be reported. Both directions, the rule the backup gate follows: an item the corpus does not
know about is as much a defect as a record the index lacks.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#37:
THE EXPECTED SET COMES FROM D1, not from the repository artifact, which meant a GitHub fetch on
every admin page load for one integer. `publishableForAsk` is still the UPLOADERS' filter and must
stay in step with the SQL predicate here; `check:policy` binds the two.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#38:
CONCURRENT, because the two sides share nothing: a D1 read and a paged walk of AI Search, neither
reading what the other writes, and they were strictly serial.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#39:
THE PAPERS ARE PART OF WHAT THE INDEX SHOULD HOLD: without this the badge would report them
permanently stale and the repair button would delete them.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#40:
The request-scoped, MEMOIZED reader for the drift status above.

Two surfaces want the same fact, and a parent cannot read a child's loader data. Moving the
computation up was ruled out because `check:admin-ui` fabricates this in the posts route's OWN
loader data, so relocating it would have moved the gate's fixture. The VALUE moves instead, on
the context, as the verified session already does. A getter, so a route that never asks never
pays.
app/lib/search/ask.server.ts#43:
THE DRIFT COUNT FOR THE NAV BADGE, off the read path, because `askIndexStatus` pages the whole
index and the admin layout runs on every admin page load.

ON A HIT THIS DOES NOT TOUCH AI SEARCH, structurally: one `return` sits between the KV read and
the first mention of the index, and `check:invariants` section 11 asserts that ordering ON THE
SOURCE rather than on a timing mark, a mark count having already proved unable to see an unmarked
read here.

FAILURE IS NULL, NOT ZERO: zero would claim the index agrees with the corpus, on no evidence,
beside a repair the operator would then not perform.

THE LATE WRITE IS A PROMISE, AND IT IS THE MECHANISM RATHER THAN AN OPTIMISATION. A floating
write lands only if the isolate outlives the response, so a listing slower than the budget never
populated the cache and the next request missed for the same reason. `waitUntil` is the fix
rather than a longer budget, because any budget has a listing slower than it, and the
ExecutionContext is REQUIRED so a call site that cannot supply it is a typecheck failure.

THE COUNT ONLY: the page that owns the repair reads the full lists uncached.
